claim: On 2023-06-13 Amazon EC2 added EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint, which lets you connect to an instance through SSH or RDP without the instance having a public IPv4 address.
question: Since when can you SSH or RDP to an instance that has no public IPv4 address without a bastion host?

evidence.quote: | [EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/connect-with-ec2-instance-connect-endpoint.html) | You can now connect to an instance through SSH or RDP without requiring the instance to have a public IPv4 address. | June 13, 2023 |

note: Best-answer change: private admin access without a bastion host or public IP.

claim: EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint lets you connect securely to an instance from the internet without a bastion host, without direct internet connectivity for the VPC and without a public IPv4 or IPv6 address on the instance.
question: How can you reach a private instance from the internet without a bastion host or a public IP address?

values.display: a public IPv4 or IPv6 address
values.spoken: the instance needs no public IP address

qualifiers.scope: instances in a VPC with an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint

evidence.quote: EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint allows you to connect securely to an instance from the internet, without using a bastion host, or requiring that your virtual private cloud (VPC) has direct internet connectivity.
You can connect to your instances without requiring the instances to have a public IPv4 or IPv6 address.

claim: On 2022-10-31 Amazon EC2 made it possible to transfer Elastic IP addresses from one AWS account to another.
question: Since when can an Elastic IP address be moved to another AWS account?

evidence.quote: | [Transfer Elastic IP addresses](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/elastic-ip-addresses-eip.html#transfer-EIPs-intro-ec2) | You can now transfer Elastic IP addresses from one AWS account to another. | October 31, 2022 |

note: Older material says an Elastic IP can't leave its account; it still can't move to another Region (ec2-eip-region-bound-ipv4-only).

claim: In February 2026 Capacity Blocks for ML gained two options: on February 2, 2026 you can share them with other accounts in your AWS organization, and on February 25, 2026 they became available in Local Zones.
question: What did the February 2026 changes add to Capacity Blocks for ML?

values.display: share EC2 Capacity Blocks with other AWS accounts
values.spoken: you can share Capacity Blocks inside your organization

qualifiers.condition: UltraServer Capacity Blocks can't be shared

evidence.quote: | [Capacity Blocks sharing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-blocks-share.html) | You can share EC2 Capacity Blocks with other AWS accounts in your AWS organization. | February 2, 2026 |
| [Capacity Blocks in Local Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-capacity-blocks.html) | Capacity Blocks for ML are now available in Local Zones. | February 25, 2026 |
UltraServer Capacity Blocks can't be shared across AWS accounts or within your AWS Organization.

claim: On 2024-11-20 Amazon EC2 made it possible to specify that instances run only in a Capacity Reservation or a Capacity Reservation resource group.
question: Since when can you require that instances launch only into a Capacity Reservation?

values.display: only run in a Capacity Reservation

evidence.quote: | [Capacity Reservations only](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-capacity-reservations.html) | You can now specify that instances will only run in a Capacity Reservation or Capacity Reservation resource group. | November 20, 2024 |
